Run `2026-10-12_1024_mcp-recipe_mistral-small-2603-high` scored **35/100**. The grade is in `grade.json` and `grade.md`, and it shows up in the report's Grade table. After `npm run reset` archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-12_1024_mcp-recipe_mistral-small-2603-high`, `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 6/35 |
| Content modeling | 23/25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 3/25 |
| Content & presentation | 1/10 |
| Process & honesty | 2/5 |

**Summary:** Mistral Small built a correct schema through the MCP servers: rich text, image and quote blocks, a block grid data type in `/Custom`, and front page and post types. It published two posts and set a `/` domain on the front page. It then wrote its Razor views in the wrong folder and added ViewComponents that don't compile. The build fails, the site never boots, and the posts describe MCP as an invented "Model-Content-Property" pattern instead of the Model Context Protocol.

**Top issues:**
1. **The build fails** with 6 errors. `Components/{RichText,Image,Quote}ViewComponent.cs` inherit a `BlockViewComponent` type that doesn't exist. Umbraco never became ready, so there are **no screenshots**: `npm run screenshot` reported "Umbraco isn't running". `grade.md` says so instead of embedding them.
2. **The views are in the wrong place.** After a stray `cd ..`, every page view and block partial went to `Umbraco.Bench/Views/` at the solution root, not into the web project. The project's own `blogFrontPage.cshtml` and `blogPost.cshtml` are still the empty template stubs.
3. **The architecture is wrong even ignoring the location.** The block partials use the wrong paths, hold all the markup and never call `Component.InvokeAsync`. There are no view models and no component views.
4. **The final report is inaccurate.** It just says "Task completed." even though the model's last `dotnet build` had failed.
5. **The post content is wrong and thin:** four short paragraphs per post, with made-up quote attributions.
6. **Minor:** `blogFrontPage` allows `siteRoot` as a child. The recipe's restart and curl checks were skipped. One `ls` of the bench root went outside the project folder.

The reset left the scaffold set up for the plain MCP test, not MCP Recipe. If the next run is another MCP Recipe run, it needs `npm run setup -- mcp-recipe` first.
